# The Farmer Companies Raises $17 Million Series A And Names Randy Johnson CEO

By Amit Chowdhry

Pulse 2.0

The Farmer Companies Raises $17 Million Series A And Names Randy Johnson CEO

Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn

The Farmer Companies has raised $17 million in Series A financing and appointed former Dot’s Pretzels CEO Randy Johnson as chief executive officer. Raff Ventures led the funding round, with participation from AJAX Capital Partners. Johnson succeeds founder Adam Farmer, who will remain actively involved as chairman.

The leadership change follows The Farmer Companies’ acquisition of WHISPS and supports its strategy of building a leading North American cheese-snacking business. [...] Randy Johnson, CEO of The Farmer Companies

Hershey acquired the business for $1.2 billion in 2021.

The Farmer Companies’ portfolio includes WHISPS Cheese Crisps and an exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery to produce Cabot Creamery Popcorn.

The company described Cabot Creamery Popcorn as the fastest-growing U.S. food popcorn brand among the 13 leading brands tracked by NielsenIQ.

Proceeds from the Series A will support manufacturing partnerships, expanded national distribution and strategic acquisitions.

Founded in 2021, The Farmer Companies acquires, builds and operates premium consumer brands, with a current focus on cheese-based snacks and related categories.

# The Farmer Companies Raises $17M in Series A Funding

FinSMEs

By FinSMEs

FacebookTwitterWhatsAppLinkedin

The Farmer Companies, a Burlington, VT-based provider of a cheese snack platform, raised $17M in Series A financing.

The round was led by Raff Ventures with participation from AJAX Capital Partners. [...] The company intends to use the funds to expand its national distribution, making strategic acquisitions, and scaling its manufacturing network across North America.

Led by CEO Randy Johnson, The Farmer Companies is a consumer packaged goods (CPG) platform and brand builder specializing in cheese-based snacking and licensed food products.

They currently operate across North America with national distribution in U.S. food retail.

In this Q&A, we speak with CEO Adam Farmer, a South Burlington local, about the company’s origins, how Cabot helped shape its journey, and what’s to come.

Blaise: Adam! Thanks for making the time. First of all, have you always been an entrepreneur? [...] Adam: As you can imagine, I had to sell a lot of Safe2S’its to even make my money back. And after four or five months of making $50 a day, I realized that I wanted to learn about raising money. So I coldcalled Merrill Lynch in Burlington. They interviewed me but I didn’t get hired because I had no experience. But they said, ‘If you get your Series 7 and Series 65, call us back.’ So me and Ben Carter – who’s now our Chief Growth Officer – both started at Northwestern Mutual in Jacksonville, working for 100% commission, and studying in our free time.
